title: Zion’s Saints are to keep the Sabbath with thanks
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Jackson County, Missouri, on 7 August 1831. In the days before, the land had been dedicated for Zion and a temple site dedicated. That morning Polly Knight, wife of Joseph Knight Sr., died, the first Church member to die there. Sunday worship was lax among local settlers, and earlier Church laws said little about the Sabbath. Joseph Smith had been told to return to Ohio, so the Saints needed written guidance.
summary: The revelation blesses those who came to Zion with an eye single to God’s glory. Those who live will inherit the earth, and those who die will rest and receive a crown. It then gives commandments to love God and neighbor and not to steal, commit adultery, or kill. It asks for thanks in all things and the sacrifice of a broken heart and contrite spirit. The Saints are to go to the house of prayer and offer their sacraments on the Lord’s day. That day they are to rest, confess their sins, and prepare food with singleness of heart. If they do these things with thanks and glad hearts, the fulness of the earth is theirs. God is offended only by those who do not confess his hand in all things and do not obey.

contextNote.title: A day to stay unspotted
contextNote.text: The Saints were building Zion among settlers who largely ignored Sunday worship. Verse 9 gives the reason for the Sabbath command: to keep oneself “unspotted from the world” more fully. The means is going to the house of prayer and offering sacraments on the holy day. Verse 10 adds that the day is set apart to rest from labor and to worship. Verses 13–14 then describe fasting as “rejoicing and prayer” with a glad heart. In this passage, keeping the Sabbath is a weekly practice that sets the Saints apart from their surroundings.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 58–59 connects Sabbath worship and gratitude. Verses 9–14 list what the Saints should do on the Lord’s day; which of those actions could you add to your next Sabbath?
reviewNote: Read all 24 verses. Official heading gives Zion, Jackson County, 7 August 1831, after dedication of land and temple site, and the death of Polly Knight that day. JSP historical introduction gave local Sabbath conditions and the gap in earlier Church law. JSP says it is unclear whether the revelation came before or after Joseph Smith learned of Polly Knight’s death. Polly Knight is not named in the text, so no new person was added; joseph-knight-sr is included for the setting. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes. Setting checked against the official heading and JSP historical introduction.
